article_title: Kotlin Toolchain 0.13 Becomes JetBrains' Recommendation for New KMP Projects as the KMP Plugin Drops Swift IDE Support

content_preview.title: Kotlin Toolchain 0.13 Becomes JetBrains' Recommendation for New KMP Projects as the KMP Plugin Drops Swift IDE Support
content_preview.summary: JetBrains now recommends the Kotlin Toolchain for most new Kotlin Multiplatform projects as v0.13 adds kotlin new and SwiftPM support, while the KMP plugin drops Swift IDE features.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

JetBrains now recommends the Kotlin Toolchain for most new Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) projects. According to the [Kotlin blog post announcing v0.13](https://blog.jetbrains.com/kotlin/2026/10/start-your-next-kmp-app-with-kotlin-toolchain-0-13/), "With the release of v0.13, we now recommend the Kotlin Toolchain for most new Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) projects." In a separate post, [JetBrains said](https://blog.jetbrains.com/kotlin/2026/10/discontinuing-swift-language-ide-support-in-th...

editor_notes.content_quality: News piece, 609 words (policy range 400-1200), title 118 chars (cap 150). Clear structure: overview, 0.13 changes, Swift IDE discontinuation, What We Don't Know. Neutral, every claim attributed to JetBrains. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both gzipped snapshots (source-0.html.gz, source-1.html.gz; HTTP 200, suspicious_patterns null for both, so no pattern hits to adjudicate). source-0 (blog.jetbrains.com 'Start Your Next KMP App With Kotlin Toolchain 0.13', Anton Makeev) confirms: 'With the release of v0.13, we now recommend the Kotlin Toolchain for most new Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) projects'; 'a unified entry point into Kotlin'; promoted to Alpha 'earlier this year'; kotlin new / kotlin init behavior; iOS simulator runtime auto-download, Xcode diagnostics; Android SDK provisioning on import and tightened namespace/application ID validation (com.example.app); SwiftPM swiftPackage and localSwiftPackage keys and swiftPMImport prefix; KTC-5422 native caches and settings.kotlin.compileIncrementally; Hot Reload MCP server and 'npx skills add kotlin/kotlin-agent-skills'; roadmap items (brew install kotlin, AI skills out of the box, Swift Export 'as it stabilizes', app store publishing) listed without dates; 'closing existing gaps, including those for existing Gradle projects, before recommending migrations'. The benchmark sentence ('In our benchmarks, AI agents already generate and maintain Kotlin Toolchain projects more reliably while consuming fewer tokens') is JetBrains' own claim and the post publishes no results; the article attributes it to JetBrains and states that no results are published. source-1 (blog.jetbrains.com 'Discontinuing Swift Language IDE Support in the Kotlin Multiplatform Plugin') confirms: starting with IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3 and Android Studio Rabbit 2 | 2026.2.2; scope 'editing, syntax highlighting, and navigation within Swift files and between Swift and Kotlin'; running iOS apps and debugging Kotlin on iOS remain supported; Swift Export and importing Swift packages into Kotlin not affected; older versions keep the functionality without updates; 'active usage was limited and steadily declining'; most iOS KMP developers prefer Xcode; AppCode-derived architecture; 'We do not currently plan to replace these features.' All direct quotes verified verbatim. Both domains are first-party and blog.jetbrains.com is on the allowlist (no allowlist change). Neither page shows a visible publication date (page timestamps 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-07 per writer); the article states no exact dates, only 'earlier this year', so nothing unsupported.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics trace to the two JetBrains posts. Title fact 1 (recommendation) is backed by source-0; title fact 2 (KMP plugin dropping Swift IDE support) by source-1; the body correctly scopes what is dropped (Swift editing, highlighting, navigation) versus what remains (run/debug on iOS, Swift Export, Swift package import). Linking the two in one headline with 'as' is temporal juxtaposition; the body does not claim a causal link, and the two posts are adjacent releases by the same author. The 'What We Don't Know' section is accurate: the migration caveat and undated roadmap are in source-0, and the absence of independent coverage is acknowledged. The internal link /article/2026-09/21-kotlin-2420-ships-with-sealed-class-swift-export-new-wasm-compilation-modes-and-an-experimental-native-compiler-image resolves to an existing published article in the correct singular form.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, vendor claims attributed ('JetBrains said', 'the company says', 'The company wrote').
editor_notes.originality: No existing coverage of Toolchain 0.13 or the Swift IDE discontinuation. Related prior Kotlin coverage (2.4.20, Compose Multiplatform 1.12) is distinct.
concerns: Title says the plugin 'Drops' Swift IDE support, but per source-1 the change starts with IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3 / Android Studio Rabbit 2 | 2026.2.2, later than the versions named in source-0 (2026.2.3 / Rabbit 1); the body states the timing accurately, so the title is a mild present-tense shorthand, not an error.
Title says 'for New KMP Projects' while the source says 'most new' KMP projects; the summary and body carry the 'most' qualifier.
recommendations: Prefer 'for Most New KMP Projects' in future headlines to mirror vendor wording.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed, policy-compliant article resting entirely on two first-party JetBrains posts that were read in full. APPROVE.
